passage:
Tuesday. On the phone, Afreen said, "I never told you not to come for Eid. You are imagining things. You are too sensitive." Zubin had the text on the screen: "Don't bother coming this year." For a moment the words on the screen felt less real than the voice. Zubin's stomach went cold.

Thursday. Zubin started a note on the phone: the date, what was said, what was written. Two lines. Writing it down felt like putting a foot on solid floor.

The following Sunday. Zubin told a cousin, who said, "Your mother did that to me over the wedding dates." Zubin sat still. The notes were enough, and Afreen did not have to say "you're right" for Zubin to trust them.

qa.q: What did the text on Zubin's screen say?
qa.a: It said, "Don't bother coming this year."

qa.q: Why did the words on the screen feel less real than the voice for a moment?
qa.a: Afreen's firm denial made Zubin doubt Zubin's own memory for a moment.

qa.q: How does the note help Zubin?
qa.a: A dated record of what was said and written gives Zubin something solid to trust, without needing Afreen's agreement.

qa.q: How does the cousin see Afreen's behaviour?
qa.a: The cousin says the mother did the same thing about the wedding dates, so the cousin sees a pattern rather than Zubin being too sensitive.

grounding: A parent denies what was said and calls the child too sensitive; the protagonist keeps notes, trusts direct experience and talks to a trusted person.
